title: developer-experience-standup-notes-2026-03-04
body:
Developer Experience — Standup / Weekly updates (notes consolidated 2026-03-02 -> 2026-03-04)

Attendees: Aisha (owner), Miguel, Jordan, Cameron, Priya (partial), interns: Sam & Lee (joining notes)
Timebox: 30m daily; this doc consolidates the last three standups and weekly async updates.

---
Summary / high-level
- Focus this sprint: ship TypeScript SDK v1.4.0 + streaming samples, finalize Python SDK docs for function-calling, and publish two quickstarts (embedding + streaming-chat).
- Two priority blockers: streaming SDK flaky reconnects (DX-342) and last-mile CI failures on docs build for python site.
- Action: pair Miguel+Jordan on streaming reconnect fix; Cameron to stabilize docs CI by EOD Fri (2026-03-06).

---
Day-by-day notes
2026-03-02 (Mon)
- Yesterday (what people worked on):
  - Aisha: reviewed release notes draft for TS SDK v1.4.0, started checklist for release blog.
  - Miguel: implemented reconnect backoff for streaming client, added unit tests (local green).
  - Jordan: prototype for sample app "notes-app" that demo's streaming + function calling.
  - Cameron: investigated docs site build failures — traced to new Sphinx extension and python package pin mismatch.
  - Priya: updated quickstart prose (embedding quickstart) with new cost/latency tips.
- Today (plans):
  - Aisha: finalize release checklist, review PRs, coordinate canary on dedicated.
  - Miguel: open PR for reconnect (PR #432), start integration test on staging runtime.
  - Jordan: polish notes-app README & add CI to deploy demo to preview env.
  - Cameron: pin sphinx dependency and test docs build locally.
- Blockers:
  - Streaming reconnect still flaky on longer sessions when switching networks (DX-342).
  - Docs build failing on CI only — local builds succeed (env mismatch).

2026-03-03 (Wed)
- Yesterday:
  - Miguel: PR created (github.com/redwood-inference/sdk/pull/432) — unit tests pass; intermittent e2e failures on staging.
  - Jordan: notes-app v0.2 includes function-calling example and minimal UI; demo ready for internal review.
  - Cameron: reproduced CI failure by matching build runner image; found that the pip cache had an old cryptography wheel causing C-extension mismatch.
  - Priya: drafted docs for python function-calling examples and added snippet for streaming-cancel use case.
- Today:
  - Miguel & Jordan doing joint e2e debugging; collecting logs from staging runtime and client telemetry.
  - Aisha prepping rollout plan: canary on hosting region us-west-2 with traffic split 5% -> 20% over 4 hours.
  - Cameron to update CI runner image and add an explicit dependency pin to fix build.
- Blockers/risks:
  - e2e test flakiness means we can't fully validate reconnect fix; need long-running soak test.
  - Release window tight if canary reveals perf regression (target to keep p50 < 120ms).

2026-03-04 (Thu)
- Yesterday:
  - Soak test started (12h) for streaming reconnect; after 6h a reconnect-related memory spike observed.
  - PR #432 updated by Miguel to include a memory cap and metrics emit; team reran soak.
  - Cameron pushed CI runner image change and pinned cryptography wheel -> docs build now green on CI for python site (PR 118).
  - Priya and Sam finished embedding quickstart draft and sample dataset (small FAQ added).
- Today:
  - Goal: green CI + soak for 24h -> if green, cut TS SDK canary release.
  - Jordan: finalize notes-app demo with streaming backpressure example and link to quickstart.
  - Aisha: coordinate with solutions-eng for canary monitor dashboards and SRE on-call.
- Blockers:
  - Memory spike under long idle->reconnect loop still present in rare cases; root cause needs deeper heap analysis (assigned to Miguel + SRE).

---
Decisions made this week
- Delay full v1.4.0 public rollout until soak test passes 24h with no memory regression. Canary OK to go for 5% traffic.
- Docs CI fixed by explicitly pinning cryptography wheel (temporary); follow-up ticket to audit other C-extension packages (DX-355).

---
Action items (owner — due)
- Miguel: complete heap profiling + reproduce memory leak locally (DX-342) — due 2026-03-06.
- Jordan: finish notes-app deployment automation + demo recording for internals — due 2026-03-05.
- Cameron: merge docs CI fix and cut python docs build release (PR 118) — done 2026-03-04.
- Aisha: draft canary monitoring runbook and slack alert playbook — due 2026-03-05.
- Priya: finalize embedding quickstart + publish on docs site (draft: /docs/quickstarts/embedding) — due 2026-03-07.
- Sam & Lee (interns): add two new code samples for streaming cancel and structured-output in TS SDK sample folder — due 2026-03-06.

---
Notes to self / follow-ups
- Need an internal eval checklist for streaming features (latency, p50/p95, reconnect rate, memory). Add to repo: docs/internal/streaming-eval-checklist.md.
- Revisit batching recommendations in quickstarts: show example config for Dedicated vs Hosted to highlight cost tradeoffs.
- Collect customer-facing examples from Solutions Eng for v1.4.0 docs (ask @Elena from solutions-eng).

---
Unresolved questions / discussion points
- Should the SDK expose a high-level reconnect policy (recommended) vs leaving it to users? Pros/cons: simplicity vs surprising resource use. Need design doc.
- Do we provide a single sample that demonstrates embeddings -> reranking -> streaming answer generation (end-to-end)? This would be high impact for marketing but will add maintenance burden.

---
Relevant links (for reviewers)
- SDK reconnect PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/sdk/pull/432
- Docs build fix PR (python): https://github.com/redwood-inference/docs/pull/118
- Jira: DX-342 (streaming reconnect memory), DX-355 (docs dependency audit)
- Internal preview of notes-app: https://preview.redwood.internal/notes-app/ (internal only)

---
Appendix: quick snippets / TODOs (scratch)
- Release checklist (short): update CHANGELOG -> bump package versions -> cut canary tag -> run soak 24h -> watch metrics -> promote or rollback.
- Quickstart TOC that needs to be on docs site:
  1) Quickstart: Text generation (TS + Py)
  2) Quickstart: Streaming chat with reconnect handling (TS)
  3) Quickstart: Embeddings + similarity search (Py)
  4) Sample: notes-app (end-to-end demo)

End of consolidated standup notes.

(Informal notes preserved: partial sentences, TODO markers, and inline reminders — this doc is a working artifact; move finalized content to docs repo when ready.)
